release_status: Verified locally end to end: all18 modules plus root, exact index,440-declaration allowed-axiom audit, official kernel replay and independent semantic audit passed. Remote publication/CI tracked separately.
status_definition: verified_repaired_scope means the precise statement and representation described in this map passed the full local build, axiom/kernel gates and independent source-to-Lean semantic audit.

metric_contract.graphs: Finite simple unweighted graphs; H and G have the same vertex type and H<=G. The weighted generality of Definition 1 is outside this implementation.
metric_contract.faults: Every simple subgraph F<=G with pointwise degree<=f is allowed, including F not contained in H. Only edges are removed.
metric_contract.distance: SimpleGraph.edist in ℕ∞, infinite on disconnected pairs.
metric_contract.equivalence: For positive integral t, IsDegreeFaultSpanner is equivalent to H<=G and every admissible F satisfying edist_(H-F)(u,v)<=t*edist_(G-F)(u,v) for all u,v.

exact_family.rigidity: Every f-DFT stretch-(2*k-1) spanner equals the constructed graph.

all_sizes_extension.constant: c_k=1/2^(k+3)>0, independent of N and f
all_sizes_extension.source_relation: Explicit completion of parameter interpolation beyond the paper’s written exact-family argument.
all_sizes_extension.excluded_scope: No unsaturated all-pairs claim with f>N for k>1.

k_one_repair.uniform_all_sizes_constant: The common c_k specializes to 1/16 at k=1; the separate complete-graph result retains 1/4.

statement_form_notes: Definitions 1 and 3 are specialized to finite simple unit-weight graphs and positive integral stretch.
Lemma 9 uses the documented point-rooted convention.
Lemma 10 composes a ShortReach endpoint theorem with the exact graph-path equivalence.
Lemma 13 uses an encoded oriented-cycle theorem and actual graph-walk assembly; final semantic audit remains required.

claims.scope: Finite simple unweighted specialization with positive integral stretch; the general weighted definition is not claimed in full. Extended distance lies in ℕ∞, with infinity for disconnected pairs.

Spanning edge-subgraph H<=G; faults F<=G, not necessarily F<=H, have degree at most f at every vertex. For t>0 the walk condition is equivalent to the all-pairs extended-distance inequality; no vertices are removed.

Exact family and arbitrarily-large graph witness for every k>=1,f>=1,N0, with real-exponent coefficient 1/4. Additional interpolation theorem constructs exactly N vertices for every k>=1,N>=2,1<=f<=N with c_k=1/2^(k+3); no unrestricted f>N claim for k>1. The all-size result expands the paper’s written proof.

Corrected dimension k>=2, represented as d+2. Canonical indexed lines are injective onto the actual affine subset-lines. Over F_p the graph has 2*p^k vertices and p^(k+1) edges; the source count is false at k=1.

Parallel means distinct lines with equal slope parameter. Transverse simple paths are walks in transverseGraph with Walk.IsPath. Point-to-point incidence edge length is twice its line-length; geometry is in dimension d+2.

Actual failure graph removes the distinguished edge from the augmented matching. The shortFailure relation is equivalent to a simple transverse path with path.length+2<=k, or line-length r satisfying 2*(r+1)<=k, including odd k and zero-length paths.

Point-rooted alternating closed walks with different point endpoints across every line occurrence and at most k line steps. Repeated slopes are grouped with multiplicity; distinct slopes are explicit in the independence result. Cycle corollary avoids the source’s line-rooted closing-seam ambiguity. No p>=k assumption.

Composed mapping: endpoint uniqueness and existence of a designated point use ShortReach; path equivalence recovers the exact source cutoff. For parallel lines their slopes agree. The designated endpoint need not be reachable; an arbitrary point of the nonempty target line handles empty reachability.
The actual undirected matching F_e union {e} has maximum degree at most one, including the protected point and line endpoints; F_e itself is an admissible degree-one fault graph.

Constructs a simple same-endpoint path with edge length at most twice the number of distinct original slopes; allowed slopes are preserved. Walks are constructed first and loops erased; zero displacement and zero-length paths are included.

Represented by an encoded oriented-cycle lemma with the distinguished reference line last, and actual graph-walk/cycle assembly in matchingGraph_long. The encoded result supplies a shortFailure edge before the reference line; the assembled result says every walk avoiding F_e union {e} between the protected endpoints has length >2*k-1. This composed representation, rather than a standalone literal all-cycles restatement, awaits semantic sign-off.

Concrete incidence graph rigidity in dimension k=d+2>=2, with no supplied geometry/obstruction assumption. The actual k=1 star also has stretch-one rigidity as a specialization of one_spanner_eq, but is not used for the density lower bound.

Vertices V×Fin f; two cloud vertices are adjacent exactly when their base vertices are adjacent. Each base edge yields a complete bipartite lift; there are no within-cloud edges. This is not the categorical product with an edgeless graph.
Corrected k>=2 subset-line family: N=2*f*p^k and M=f^2*p^(k+1), with 2^(k+1)*M^k=f^(k-1)*N^(k+1). General cloud edge multiplication is exact. The erroneous source k=1 incidence count is not asserted.

Lift the full base matching F_e union {e}, then exempt only the protected lifted edge. After deleting that edge too, survivingProjection maps every surviving edge outside the full base matching, including e.
The lifted fault graph has degree at most |Fin f|=f because the base augmented fault graph has degree at most one. Holds for every positive integer f; no primality or rounding requirement on f.

Actual incidence cloud graph rigidity for k>=2 and every positive f, without assumed geometric premises in the concrete theorem. Projection avoids the protected base edge; loop erasure in matchingGraph_long justifies the simple-cycle contradiction. Disconnected endpoints are covered by the metric contract.

implementation_extensions.purpose: Large-regime nearby prime and integer-power comparison
implementation_extensions.scope: For k>=2,f>=1,N>=2^(k+1)*f, constructs prime p with Nprime<=N<=2^k*Nprime. Arithmetic covers both sparse and dense regimes with common factor 2^(k+3).
For every N>=2,1<=f<=N: actual N-vertex graph, degree<=f, N*f<=4*|E(G)|, and every f-DFT spanner equals G for any natural stretch. Full K_(f+1) blocks plus isolated remainder; K_N when f=N.
Embedding a nonempty forcing graph into Fin N preserves exact edge count and edge forcing. Admissible faults extend; extra vertices are isolated. Nonemptiness is supplied for the prime family.
For k>=1 and positive integer factor A, converts f^(k-1)*N^(k+1)<=A^k*M^k to M>=(1/A)*f^(1-1/k)*N^(1+1/k).
Constructs exactly N vertices for each k>=1,N>=2,1<=f<=N and explicit c_k=1/2^(k+3). No assumed prime proximity, padded graph, dense witness, or geometry premise remains.

corrections.issue: At k=1 every affine subset-line is F_p; the actual incidence graph is K_(p,1), with p+1 vertices and p edges. Its f-cloud blowup has (p+1)*f vertices and p*f^2 edges.
corrections.repair: Use incidence-size and density arguments only for k>=2; use complete graphs for the k=1 part of Theorem 5.

clarifications: Point-rooted closed-walk convention and explicit repeated-slope grouping.
Matching includes the protected edge and has zero fault degree at its point endpoint.
Walk construction followed by loop erasure preserves allowed slopes.
Lifted projection avoids the whole base matching including the protected base edge.
Exact prime family is separate from the conventional all-size range 1<=f<=N.

background_scope: Theorems 2 and 4 are cited external results, not dependencies of the new lower-bound proof. They, their weighted upper bounds and conditional girth-conjecture assertions, and the bibliography/survey are not claimed formalized.
